$comment: The migrations that have actually been applied to the production Supabase
project (botanique-admin, ref wcacyfyxjiysfibuuhgf).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Vercel deploys the frontend automatically on every
merge to main. Nothing deploys Supabase migrations. PR #98 and PR #99 shipped
frontend code that read fund_releases and fund_acquittals to production while
those tables did not exist there, and the only symptom was a runtime error in
front of the Founder. PR #100 applied the missing migration by hand. This
ledger makes that class of mismatch fail the build instead of the user.
RECONCILE BY NAME, NOT BY VERSION. Supabase stamps its own timestamp when a
migration is applied through the dashboard or MCP, so the hosted version does
not match the repository filename prefix. The name after the prefix is the
stable key, and it is what this ledger and scripts/check-migration-drift.mjs
compare on. `productionVersion` is recorded for traceability only.
HOW TO UPDATE. Only after the migration is genuinely applied to production:
add its entry here, in apply order, with the version Supabase reports for it.
Editing this file does not apply anything — it only records what someone
already did. See docs/ui-authority/operations-hub/MIGRATION-DEPLOYMENT.md.
SPLIT APPLICATION, 12 Aug 2026. project_cost_payments was applied in five
the whole file in one call exceeded the deployment tool's request timeout. The
first attempt timed out and rolled back cleanly, creating nothing — verified
before retrying. The parts were applied in file order, each boundary chosen so
an interrupted run would fail closed: tables and RLS first with no policies or
grants, then functions, then triggers, then policies and grants last. The final
schema was verified object by object and equals the single-file migration.
productionVersion below records the FIRST of those versions.
SPLIT APPLICATION, 12 Aug 2026 (second). project_cost_historical_settlement
was applied in four transactions (versions 20260812203621, 203658, 203729,
203758) for the same reason. The boundaries fail closed: columns, the audit
table and RLS first with no policies or grants; then the settlement functions;
then the payment and cancellation guards; then the read model together with
every policy, revoke and grant. The read model is dropped and recreated to add
a column, so it was deliberately kept in the same transaction as its grant,
leaving no window in which the live register could read an ungranted function.
productionVersion below records the FIRST of those versions.
